responses.sql: SELECT s.insurstat AS insurance_status, COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref) AS conserved_sites, CAST(COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref)) OVER () AS share FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY s.insurstat

assumptions.assumption: "Conserved sites" means distinct sites that have at least one conservation record, so each site is counted once per status even if it has several records.
A missing status means a NULL insurstat. NULL forms its own group, which GROUP BY does by default. Empty strings are not treated as missing.
The share is the group's count divided by the sum of the group counts, as a real-valued fraction (0 to 1) with no rounding.

alternatives.interpretation: Count conservation records (matched rows) per insurance status instead of distinct sites. A site with several records is counted several times.
alternatives.sql: SELECT s.insurstat AS insurance_status, COUNT(*) AS conserved_sites, CAST(COUNT(*) AS REAL) / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY s.insurstat

responses.sql: SELECT s.insurstat AS insurstat, COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref) AS conserved_sites, COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT c.zoneref)) OVER () AS share FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY s.insurstat

assumptions.assumption: "Count the conserved sites" means the number of distinct sites with at least one conservation record, so COUNT(DISTINCT zoneref) per status. A site has one insurance status, so the distinct counts add up to the number of distinct conserved sites.
A missing insurstat is NULL. GROUP BY puts NULLs in one group, and that group is shown with a NULL status rather than a label.
The share is the status count divided by the sum of the per-status counts, as a decimal fraction (0 to 1) with no rounding.
An inner join is used. The foreign key guarantees every conservation record has a matching site.

alternatives.interpretation: Count conservation records per status instead of distinct sites, so a site with several records is counted several times.
alternatives.sql: SELECT s.insurstat AS insurstat, COUNT(*) AS conservation_records, COUNT(*) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(*)) OVER () AS share FROM scanconservation c JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = c.zoneref GROUP BY s.insurstat

responses.sql: SELECT s.insurstat AS insurstat, COUNT(DISTINCT sc.zoneref) AS site_count, COUNT(DISTINCT sc.zoneref) * 1.0 / SUM(COUNT(DISTINCT sc.zoneref)) OVER () AS share FROM scanconservation sc JOIN sites s ON s.zoneregistry = sc.zoneref GROUP BY s.insurstat

assumptions.assumption: "Conserved sites" means distinct sites that have at least one conservation record, so each site is counted once per status even if it has several records.
A missing status is a NULL insurstat, and GROUP BY puts NULLs in their own group. Empty strings are not treated as missing.
The share is each count divided by the sum of all counts, as a decimal fraction between 0 and 1 with no rounding. Multiplying by 1.0 avoids integer division.
